text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov recommended to postpone opening of secret police files from the communist era until the Constitutional Court rules on an appeal by 52 opposition deputies agains parts of the respective law which they said contravened the constitution.
The law for opening the files was approved by parliament at the end of July. @
-- Bulgaria's state Post Bank said it had posted 12.3 billion levs net profit for the first half of this year.
-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose to 605 billion levs at the end of July from 429.9 billion levs on July 17, a Finance Ministry official said.

-- Bulgaria is expected to call a tender for the construction of the Bulgarian stretch of the projected oil pipeline to carry Russian oil from the Bulgarian Black Sea port of Bourgas to Alexandroupolis in Greece, deputy Prime minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said.

-- Local retail traders were expected to boost supply of Bulgarian made cheese after Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said the government will lift customs fees for the import of 3,000 tonnes of cheese in a bid to curb unjustified price rises in the past two weeks, Sofia Commodity Exchange brokers said. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
